messages:
jordan (Support): heads up — customer GoodFoods Inc opened INC-4532. Their Dedicated capacity dashboard for cluster gf-prod-eu-west1 shows 0 nodes / 0 GPUs after they performed a nodepool rename + label migration. They still have running workloads on GPUs. Can SRE triage?

tara (GoodFoods): we renamed gpu-nodes-v2 -> gpu-prod-e at ~12:32 UTC and applied an annotation migration script. UI dropped rows at ~12:35. kubectl get nodes shows GPUs present.

alex (On-call SRE): can you paste the exact node labels/annotations from one node? also is prometheus scraping the nodes?

jordan (Support): pasted from customer: ``kubelet.kubernetes.io/hostname=gpu-001, nvidia.com/gpu.present=true, redwood.pool= (empty after migration), cluster.k8s.io/nodepool=gpu-prod-e``

maria (Eng-SRE): initial hypothesis: inventory ETL maps nodes to Dedicated pools using label `redwood.pool`. If that label was removed during migration we might drop rows instead of falling back. I'll tail telemetry agent logs now.

maria (Eng-SRE): running: ``kubectl -n redwood-telemetry logs telemetry-agent-gf -f``

maria (Eng-SRE): log snippet:
```
2026-03-01T12:35:02Z ERROR inventory/collector.go:142 missing label "redwood.pool" on node gpu-001, skipping node mapping
2026-03-01T12:35:02Z WARN telemetry/exporter.go:88 no pool mapping for node gpu-001, skipping capacity event
```

samir (Support Lead): customer is asking if this affects billing or reserved capacity charges. do we have any billing telemetry?

jordan (Support): billing dashboard still shows reserved capacity for GoodFoods, no spike. problem looks visual/analytics only. customer wants reassurance and a fix.

maria (Eng-SRE): confirmed prometheus still scrapes node metrics (node_exporter up), but our inventory ETL dropped those nodes from the pool table. repro steps so far: 1) rename nodepool (annotation) 2) run label-migration script that clears `redwood.pool` 3) inventory job runs and removes nodes without `redwood.pool`.

jess (Product PM): we should tolerate nodepool->annotation migrations. short-term: accept `cluster.k8s.io/nodepool` and node annotations as fallback. long-term: make mapping resilient to label churn.

maria (Eng-SRE): quick mitigation: change ETL to accept `cluster.k8s.io/nodepool` OR `redwood.pool` for mapping. deploying patch to staging first.

---
maria (Eng-SRE): staging patch logs:
```
INFO inventory/collector.go: mapping via annotation cluster.k8s.io/nodepool=gpu-prod-e
INFO telemetry/exporter.go: emitting capacity event for pool gpu-prod-e
```
---

maria (Eng-SRE): deploy-bot triggered prod rollout: ``/deploy inventory-etl v2.3.1 --prod``
deploy-bot: rollout started for inventory-etl v2.3.1

maria (Eng-SRE): prod rollout complete. backfill job started to repopulate pool table.

jordan (Support): customer reports UI repopulated at ~12:46 UTC, nodes and GPU rows restored. they confirm workloads unaffected.

maria (Eng-SRE): root cause: label migration cleared `redwood.pool` and ETL treated absence as definitive removal. Fix: fallback to nodepool annotation; added backfill + regression test for label/annotation migration cases.

samir (Support Lead): will update INC-4532 with RCA and resolution steps. customer asked for a postmortem doc. jess can you own the follow-up with product?

jess (Product PM): yep — I'll draft a short postmortem and schedule a doc update for operator runbooks.

jordan (Support): closing loop with customer. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: incident tags updated: incident=INC-4532 severity=low status=resolved
